cat > Cargo.toml <<'EOF'
[package]
name = "wintool"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
description = "Windows-only tool using direct Win32 API bindings"
publish = false

# Only pull in Windows bindings when targeting Windows.
[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies.windows]
version = "0.62"
# The `windows` crate is split into feature-gated namespaces; enable only what you use
# to keep compile times down. Find the feature for any API at:
# https://microsoft.github.io/windows-rs/features
features = [
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_System_SystemInformation",
    "Win32_System_Threading",
    "Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging",
]

[profile.release]
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
strip = true
EOF
mkdir -p .cargo && cat > .cargo/config.toml <<'EOF'
# Default to the Windows target so `cargo check`/`cargo build` work the same
# from any host. Override with `--target` if needed.
[build]
target = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"

# Statically link the C runtime so the .exe has no VC++ redistributable dependency.
[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
rustflags = ["-C", "target-feature=+crt-static"]
EOF
cat > rust-toolchain.toml <<'EOF'
[toolchain]
channel = "stable"
targets = ["x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
EOF
cat > src/main.rs <<'EOF'
#[cfg(not(windows))]
compile_error!("wintool only supports Windows targets (e.g. x86_64-pc-windows-msvc).");

use windows::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GetSystemInfo, SYSTEM_INFO};
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcessId;
use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{MB_ICONINFORMATION, MB_OK, MessageBoxW};
use windows::core::{HSTRING, w};

fn main() -> windows::core::Result<()> {
    let pid = unsafe { GetCurrentProcessId() };

    let mut info = SYSTEM_INFO::default();
    unsafe { GetSystemInfo(&mut info) };

    let text = HSTRING::from(format!(
        "PID: {pid}\nLogical processors: {}\nPage size: {} bytes",
        info.dwNumberOfProcessors, info.dwPageSize
    ));
    println!("{text}");

    unsafe { MessageBoxW(None, &text, w!("wintool"), MB_OK | MB_ICONINFORMATION) };
    Ok(())
}
EOF

content.text:
I set up a new Rust project called `wintool` in `/work`. You didn't give a name, so I picked one; change it in `Cargo.toml` if you want something else. `cargo check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass when targeting `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. I couldn't link or run it because this machine is Linux.

**What's in it**

- **`Cargo.toml`**: uses Microsoft's official [`windows`](https://crates.io/crates/windows) crate (0.62), and only on Windows targets. The crate is split into optional feature groups; I turned on just the ones the sample code needs (`Win32_Foundation`, `SystemInformation`, `Threading`, `WindowsAndMessaging`). When you use a new API, look up its feature at https://microsoft.github.io/windows-rs/features. Release builds are set up for small, fast executables (LTO, one codegen unit, stripped).
- **`.cargo/config.toml`**: builds for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` by default, so `cargo build` targets Windows whatever machine you're on. It also links the C runtime statically, so the `.exe` doesn't need the Visual C++ redistributable installed.
- **`rust-toolchain.toml`**: pins stable Rust with clippy, rustfmt and the Windows target, so anyone cloning it gets the same setup automatically.
- **`src/main.rs`**: a minimal example that calls `GetCurrentProcessId`, `GetSystemInfo` and `MessageBoxW` directly. It includes a `compile_error!` so building for any non-Windows target fails straight away with a clear message.

**Things to know**

- **Building a real `.exe`:** do it on Windows with the MSVC build tools installed. From Linux you could use `cargo-xwin`, or switch to the `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` target with mingw. Cross-platform `cargo check` already works.
- **Alternative crate:** if you'd rather have the thinnest possible raw C-style bindings (no `Result` wrappers, faster compiles), use `windows-sys` instead. Its feature names work the same way.
- **The pop-up:** the sample opens a message box. If this is a console tool, delete that call and its import.

Nothing is committed yet. The repo is on `master` and your main branch is `main`, so tell me which branch you want before I commit. `Cargo.lock` should be committed too, since this is an application.

# Statically link the C runtime so the .exe has no VC++ redistributable dependency.
[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
rustflags = ["-C", "target-feature=+crt-static"]
EOF
cat > rust-toolchain.toml <<'EOF'
[toolchain]
channel = "stable"
targets = ["x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
EOF
cat > src/main.rs <<'EOF'
#[cfg(not(windows))]
compile_error!("wintool only supports Windows targets (e.g. x86_64-pc-windows-msvc).");

use windows::Win32::System::SystemInformation::{GetSystemInfo, SYSTEM_INFO};
use windows::Win32::System::Threading::GetCurrentProcessId;
use windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging::{MB_ICONINFORMATION, MB_OK, MessageBoxW};
use windows::core::{HSTRING, w};

fn main() -> windows::core::Result<()> {
    let pid = unsafe { GetCurrentProcessId() };

    let mut info = SYSTEM_INFO::default();
    unsafe { GetSystemInfo(&mut info) };

    let text = HSTRING::from(format!(
        "PID: {pid}\nLogical processors: {}\nPage size: {} bytes",
        info.dwNumberOfProcessors, info.dwPageSize
    ));
    println!("{text}");

    unsafe { MessageBoxW(None, &text, w!("wintool"), MB_OK | MB_ICONINFORMATION) };
    Ok(())
}
EOF
